name: One Handed Keyboard
shortDescription: Wrist-mounted keyboard for one hand: 5 buttons, sequence decoding and trie + fuzzy-search word prediction on STM32, sent over UART.
description:
An AAC (augmentative and alternative communication) device for mobility-limited users: a wrist-mounted keyboard that types with simple button sequences and predictive text, built for ECE 198.

Highlights:
- Full typing with only 5 GPIO buttons: the wrist-side STM32 decodes button sequences into letters and actions.
- Word prediction combines a trie with fuzzy search over Google's 10,000 most common words, so words can be entered by shortcut.
- A transmitter that sends over UART across more than a meter to a base-station STM32, which drives an LCD.
- Housing designed in CAD and 3D-printed for stability while typing and adjustable fit; wiring plans in Altium Designer; firmware in STM32Cube.
- The submission received a 99% overall grade, with full written documentation.

Repos: [`SeqKeyTransmitter`](https://github.com/ANonABento/SeqKeyTransmitter) (wrist-side firmware) · [`SeqKeyReceiver`](https://github.com/ANonABento/SeqKeyReceiver) (base-station firmware).
